gradeScale: Sound and Overall scores on a 1-10 scale with dimensional ratings (Bass, Mids, Treble, X-Factor, Comfort, Value).

entries.name: Hifiman Susvara
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 7.1/10, overall 7.2/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6, Treble 8, X-Factor 8.5, Comfort 7.5, Value 3.3) (MSRP $6,000).
entries.quote: Highly detailed, highly revealing sound signature that emphasizes clarity. Could use a bass shelf

entries.name: Focal Utopia
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 7/10, overall 6.3/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 6, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 4, Value 3.6) (MSRP $4,400).
entries.quote: Vivid, incisive and extremely punchy sound, forward midrange flaring effect

entries.name: Aune AR9000
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 7/10, overall 7.3/10 (Bass 8, Mids 8.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 6, Comfort 8, Value 5) (MSRP $1,399).
entries.quote: A natural evolution on the Focal sound signature, with better bass extension and low end presence. Relaxed and versatile.

entries.name: Sennheiser HE 1 Orpheus 2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.8/10, overall 7.3/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 9, Value 1) (MSRP $60,000).
entries.quote: Really good bass presentation for an e-stat, it's slightly dipped in the ear gain, similar to the HD 800 S, but well balanced for the rest of it.

entries.name: HEDDPhone D1
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.5/10, overall 6.7/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7.5, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 7.5, Value 5.5) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: A neutral headphone that's the closest thing to an upgraded HD 600, benefits from a bass boost

entries.name: Hifiman Susvara Unveiled
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.5/10, overall 6.7/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 7, Treble 6, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 7.5, Value 2.8) (MSRP $8,000).
entries.quote: Similar to Susvara, just more filled in midrange but stronger lower treble emphasis, again benefits from a bass boost

entries.name: Stax SR-007
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.4/10, overall 6.5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 7, X-Factor 7, Comfort 7, Value 4.4) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: One of the more balanced sounding electrostatic headphones out there, probably the best one if you're not a treble-head. Still very incisive.

entries.name: HEDD Audio HEDDphone D1
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.4/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 7, X-Factor 8, Comfort 2, Value 4.8) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: Well balanced and highly detailed presentation with good lateral definition, just with an occasional boxy midrange modal feature on some units

entries.name: ZMF Caldera
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.4/10, overall 6.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5.5, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 5, Value 3.6) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Flat but elevated low frequency extension, giving a warm, thicker presentation overall, with somewhat dipped ear gain. Colored, but pleasant, incisive and non-fatiguing.

entries.name: Focal Utopia 2022
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.4/10, overall 5.9/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 4, Value 3.5) (MSRP $4,400).
entries.quote: A warmer take on the Utopia. It's good but not as vivid and expressive as the original

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE1000 Unveiled
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 6.4/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6, Treble 6, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 7, Value 3.6) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Too bright for me without EQ but extremely revealing and spacious sounding

entries.name: HIFIMAN Arya Unveiled
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 6.4/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6, Treble 6, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 7, Value 4.8) (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Too much 5khz, but otherwise great treble balance. Recommended with a bass boost

entries.name: HEDDphone 2 GT
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7, Treble 5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 5, Value 4.3) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: Mostly balanced sound signature with a bit of forward mid bass bloom and some extra upper treble

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 480 Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 6.7/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 7, Treble 7, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 8, Value 6.4) (MSRP $399).
entries.quote: Extremely solid mids and treble, only held back by mediocre bass quality. But otherwise this is the new default go-to recommendation for closed back headphones.

entries.name: DCA Aeon Core
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 6.2/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 6, Value 5.4) (MSRP $899).
entries.quote: Possibly the best closed-back planar. A more reserved take on the Harmanlike sound signature, in a tasteful way. Slightly cold lower midrange but smooth and well balanced otherwise.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-4
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.2/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7, Treble 4, X-Factor 8, Comfort 1, Value 3.6) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Some of the better bass and midrange balance overall, and a very incisive presentation, but also quite dark in certain regions of the treble.

entries.name: Modhouse Tungsten DS V2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.1/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 3, Value 4.3) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: Works best for me with the warmer tuned pads, there's a bit of a mid treble peak on this one but nicely balanced otherwise. Similar to certain HiFiMAN headphones.

entries.name: Focal Clear
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.1/10, overall 5.9/10 (Bass 7.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 5, Value 5.5) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: Extremely punchy sounding, hits like a truck. Similar vivid presentation to the Utopia just with a grittier, less refined treble presentation

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio E3
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 6, Value 4.4) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: A good closed-back all-rounder, it's got a bit of flare in a couple of spots throughout the bass and treble for me but that's likely just the variability of the AMTS showing up.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 600
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.9/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 7.5, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 6.6) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Great for natural, normal tonal balance with a hint of sweetness and flare to keep it interesting. Awesome for vocals

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 550
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 6.2/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 7, Treble 6.5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 7, Value 6.4) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Just really well balanced overall with some of the best midrange available, just with a slightly gritty treble presence to it.

entries.name: Austrian Audio Composer
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 6.5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 6, X-Factor 6, Comfort 8, Value 4) (MSRP $2,700).
entries.quote: Solid all around, with a dip in the early portion of the ear gain and slightly extra upper treble. Suede pads don't change much but they may change more for big heads.

entries.name: Focal Bathys MG
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 6, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 4.7) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: Sounds best in Dynamic mode, which is a pleasant, balanced presentation. Default mode has a more forward low mid section that has a bit too much bloom for me

entries.name: Moondrop Cosmo
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.7/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 6, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 5, Value 5.2) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Very unique sound signature that's both slightly dark and slightly lean, with a forward character in the midrange. Possibly one of the most capable planar drivers available, and is exceptional at pad swapping.

entries.name: Meze Empyrean II
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 6.5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 6, X-Factor 7, Comfort 8, Value 3.9) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: A v-shaped sounding planar that does a better job of balancing ear gain with mid and upper treble than the previous iteration. Great build and comfort too.

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE1000 Stealth
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 6, X-Factor 7, Comfort 6, Value 5.2) (MSRP $949).
entries.quote: Too much upper treble but one of the more balanced HE1000 series headphones, still has the ear gain dip but more coherent than previous iterations

entries.name: Warwick Acoustics Bravura
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.9/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 6, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5.5, Value 3.1) (MSRP $6,300).
entries.quote: Harmanlike sound signature in an estat. It's not quite as incisive or revealing as some other e-stats, but well balanced and solid all around

entries.name: ZMF Caldera Closed
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.7/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 5, Value 3.6) (MSRP $3,700).
entries.quote: Wonky ear gain presentation that somehow just seems to work for me every time I listen to it. Highly incisive without being fatiguing

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE6
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 7, Mids 4.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 3, Value 4.8) (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Very punchy and intense sounding planar. Default pads are quite wonky in the mids, but works well with Sundara pads to reclaim some sense of timbral normalcy

entries.name: Focal Elex
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.8/10 (Bass 7, Mids 6.5, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 5, Value 6) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Very similar to the Clear, slightly brighter leaning, depending on the unit

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 650
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 5.8/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 7.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 6.4) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: The warmer equivalent to the HD 600. It's too warm for me once the pads wear in but with fresh pads it's just about right.

entries.name: ZMF Auteur
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 6.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 4.7) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: Perhaps still my favorite ZMF. Natural, balanced sound with good timbre, not quite as incisive as others but also quite spacious sounding

entries.name: Audeze Maxwell
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 5.7/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 5, Comfort 5, Value 6.6) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Great balance overall, minor forwardness in ear gain

entries.name: Hifiman He6seV2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 5.5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 6, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 4, Value 6.3) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: A more timbrally appropriate and balanced sounding take on the HE6, just not quite as vivid or colorful as the original

entries.name: Hifiman Edition XV
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 5.9/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 6.3) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: A warmer / darker alternative to the Edition XS, with similar characteristics like good bass extension and 2khz dip.

entries.name: Hifiman HE600
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 5.7/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 5, Value 5.4) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: More like a Sundara+ than a true HE6 successor, but that's probably a good thing since it's more normal for its timbre. Slightly forward in the low treble but otherwise solid all around.

entries.name: Focal Hadenys
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 6.1/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6.5, Value 5.7) (MSRP $650).
entries.quote: An open-back HD 600-like headphone with a bass boost, the only downside is a slight 3.5khz peak that causes a timbral shift.

entries.name: Warwick Acoustics Aperio
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.9/10, overall 5.8/10 (Bass 7, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 9, Comfort 5.5, Value 1) (MSRP $40,000).
entries.quote: A more colored and esoteric sound signature, strangely intimate, but also extremely incisive and revealing for certain recordings. Works great for jazz.

entries.name: Stax SR-X9000
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 5.8/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 6, X-Factor 8, Comfort 6, Value 3) (MSRP $6,200).
entries.quote: E-stat that curbs the timbral insanity of the other stax models while still staying detailed and incisive

entries.name: Sennheiser HD800s
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 6.5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 9, Value 4.7) (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Spacious sound at the cost of being a bit on the shrill side at times. But it does sound detailed and effortless for certain recordings.

entries.name: FiiO FT7
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.7/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 4, Value 5.6) (MSRP $699).
entries.quote: Two sound signatures with different pads, the cloth ones worked best for me. Sounds good but some driver modal issues so expect unit variation

entries.name: Audeze MM-500
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.7/10, overall 4.5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 7, Treble 4.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 1, Value 4.5) (MSRP $1,700).
entries.quote: A slightly dark yet mostly balance presentation, good mids just with a forward upper mid and ear gain presence to it. Aggressive clamp, not at all suitable for big heads.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-X (2021)
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 5.6/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 6, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 4.9) (MSRP $1,200).
entries.quote: Similar to GX just with a bit better treble. Overall it's also got the relaxed anti-shout sound signature, but that also means it's not quite as clarity focused.

entries.name: ASUS ROG Kithara (ASUS Kithara (Velour))
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 6.1/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 7.5, Value 6.3) (MSRP $359).
entries.quote: Slightly on the lean and bright side, but not overtly fatiguing, with a decent balance overall.

entries.name: Thieaudio Cypher
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 3.5, Mids 7.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 6.2) (MSRP $399).
entries.quote: Shockingly good midrange, but slightly softer bass and treble with just a hint of shout. Anti V-shape headphone that's great for anyone who is sensitive to treble resonances.

entries.name: Stax SR-L700
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 5.8/10 (Bass 3, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 9, Comfort 7, Value 4.5) (MSRP $1,650).
entries.quote: Super wonky tuning, almost W-shaped sound, but also some kind of magic with the right tracks. Crazy detailed

entries.name: Final D8000 Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 4.8/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 4, Treble 5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 2, Value 3.3) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: A bass and treble focused presentation, solid punchy bass but with shifted ear gain away from 3khz.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-2F
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 7.5, Comfort 4, Value 5.1) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Warm and thick low frequency presentation, relaxed ear gain lacking a bit of clarity, and somewhat esoteric upper treble. But it's incisive and enjoyable overall.

entries.name: Sony MDR-MV1
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 6.4/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 8.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 9, Value 6.2) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: One of the better V-shaped headphones available - it's bass and treble emphasized but still smooth, great for gaming. The only downside is a 6khz peak.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-5
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 4.5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 7, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 1, Value 3.3) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: On the one hand, extremely clarity focused for the mids and upper mids. On the other hand, a bit shouty and glaring for certain types of music with not enough treble to balance it out.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-R70xa
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 5, Mids 7, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 3, Value 6.3) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Great mids, okayish bass and treble. Similar to original R70X just with worse mechanical design.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 505
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.8/10 (Bass 4.5, Mids 7, Treble 5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 7, Value 6.6) (MSRP $280).
entries.quote: A leaner take on the HD 550, but similar strengths / weaknesses. Solid all around

entries.name: FiiO FT1 Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 6.9) (MSRP $220).
entries.quote: Decent balance all around, slightly forward ear gain but solid timbre for a planar. Note, excursion limited, not a good candidate for EQ

entries.name: ZMF Bokeh Closed (2024, Black Limba)
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.6/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 5) (MSRP $1,099).
entries.quote: Fairly normal and inoffensive sound signature with a low mid emphasis.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Aeon 2 Noire
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 5.2) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Somewhat quirky low treble presentation but otherwise decent tonal balance with a good sense of detail and incisiveness

entries.name: ZMF Verite Closed
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 6, Value 4.3) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: A lush, rich presentation that's also hard hitting, the main downside is a low treble peak around 5khz that consistently shows up on my head.

entries.name: Meze Elite
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.4/10, overall 6/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 8, Value 3.5) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Odd measuring but lush and inviting sound signature. Relaxed ear gain, but still internally coherent. My main issue with it is the upper treble being too forward still.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Aeon X Closed
entries.rawName: Dan Clark Audio Aeon X Closed
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.4/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 6.2) (MSRP $399).
entries.quote: A well balanced closed back all around provided you get a good seal.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 270 Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.4/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 4, Value 7.4) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Massive bass, forward upper mids, forward treble. Sounds like if the contrast slider is turned up on the image a bit to much.

entries.name: Sennheiser hdb 630
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.4/10, overall 5.6/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 5.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 5.9) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: A decently tuned ANC headphone with PEQ in the app. Mild treble peak on my head and forward ear gain but can be fixed with the app.

entries.name: Fiio FT1
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.4/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 4, Value 7.1) (MSRP $180).
entries.quote: Currently the budget closed back headphone to beat, great bass and midrange, slightly dark ear gain and treble.

entries.name: Abyss JOAL
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.4/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 3, Value 4.3) (MSRP $1,900).
entries.quote: The most balanced sounding Abyss headphone. Has a bit of a hole around 4khz but otherwise rather pleasant. Not suitable for large heads due to mechanical design choices

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Noire X
entries.rawName: Dan Clark Audio Noire X Open
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 6, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 5) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Same issue as the closed back, but still by far the best of the DCA open backs.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Noire X
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 6, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 5) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: This would've been a really good evolution of this platform, since everything gets refined in a positive direction, except it's too forward between 2-3khz, making vocals sound a bit too intense.

entries.name: Focal Bathys
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 6, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 5.5) (MSRP $700).
entries.quote: The main issue with the Bathys is that it has quite variable behavior around 1.5khz. On some heads it'll sound totally fine but on others it'll have some honk to it. Otherwise enjoyable and incisive.

entries.name: HyperX Cloud IIIS Wireless
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 7.1) (MSRP $179).
entries.quote: A great all rounder headphone that's a little bit V-shaped but still has good balance for the mids.

entries.name: Focal Celestee
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 5) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Incisive and somewhat intimate, Harmanlike sound signature. There's a lot to like about this, just that it clamps a bit hard.

entries.name: Focal Radiance
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 4.7) (MSRP $1,300).
entries.quote: Some units of this were exceptional, other units had unhinged levels of bass and were way too boomy for me. But the good ones sound like a slightly better Celestee

entries.name: RAAL SR1a
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 2, Mids 4, Treble 6, X-Factor 8, Comfort 5, Value 3.4) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Almost DF-like mids with a forward 2khz presence, making it a bit lean, but also very detailed sounding. Bass rolls off with this kind of design

entries.name: Sennheiser HD490 Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 6.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 9, Value 6.2) (MSRP $380).
entries.quote: A baby HD 800 S. Great bass extension and presence, a bit of extra treble and the typical soundstage dip around 2khz.

entries.name: Stax SR-L300
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 2, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 8, Comfort 6, Value 6) (MSRP $450).
entries.quote: Similar to the L700, everything about this should be wrong, but there's some kind of magic with this e-stat presentation. Still, it's too wonky for its tonality to enjoy much music.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-R70x
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 5, Mids 8, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 6.3) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Exceptional midrange, just slightly unrefined and non-incisive treble presence. Very spacious sounding though.

entries.name: AKG K371
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 6, Mids 7, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 7.3) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Overall acceptable balance. Decent mids, strong sub bass, strident treble, leading to less detailed sound. Not great build

entries.name: Denon AH-D2000
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 7) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Similar to the D1001, this was a great sounding closed back for its time

entries.name: Focal Clear Mg
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 5, Value 4.5) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: A bit smoother than the Clear OG without the 6khz peak, but then introduces some other peaks higher up in frequency

entries.name: Audeze LCD-3
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 4, Value 4.2) (MSRP $1,945).
entries.quote: Odd lower treble but the recent LCD-3s have been some of the more balanced of this style of Audeze headphone

entries.name: Abyss Diana TC
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 4.7/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 3, Value 3.3) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: Similar kind of Diana sound signature just with a slightly odd upper mid timbre and dip around 4khz. Highly variable depending on positioning

entries.name: Auribus Acoustics Sierra
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.2/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 5.1) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Open back with a bass shelf and some slightly spicy, gritty treble presentation to it. But not outright offensive

entries.name: Focal Stellia
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 4, Mids 3.5, Treble 6, X-Factor 6.5, Comfort 6, Value 3.7) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: The most vivid and colored of Focal's closed-back lineup. Strange mids and somewhat bulbous bass, but treble can be highly detailed sounding

entries.name: Focal Azurys
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 6, Value 5.7) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Depends heavily on clamp pressure for seal. With a seal it's a solid closed back with a similar presentation to the Hadenys.

entries.name: Moondrop Venus
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 5, Value 5.7) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Similar sound signature to many HiFiMAN headphones, though it's a bit lean for me given its downsloping low frequency extension

entries.name: Sennheiser Momentum 5 TWS
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 6, Value 6.1) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: V-shaped bass and treble focused consumer tuning, but still retains proportional balance. Better ANC than the others but not as good sounding as HDB630

entries.name: HarmonicDyne ZEUS
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 6.2) (MSRP $379).
entries.quote: V-shaped, but also detailed. Kind of like a less grainy X2HR, just somewhat hollow sounding mids.

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE1000 V2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 6, Value 4.7) (MSRP $1,300).
entries.quote: Good bass extension, typical HiFiMAN dip in the mids and then some forward yet mostly balanced treble

entries.name: Apple AirPods Max
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 4.7/10 (Bass 7, Mids 5.5, Treble 4, X-Factor 4.5, Comfort 3, Value 5.6) (MSRP $599).
entries.quote: Minor improvements with tightened up ear gain and treble compared to the original Airpods Max, but still a bit of a grain silo in the treble

entries.name: Stax SR-009S
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 3, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 8, Comfort 7, Value 3.4) (MSRP $3,800).
entries.quote: Just too bright. It is incisive, but there are too many treble peaks in odd spots for me.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-XC
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 4.1/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 7, Comfort 1, Value 4.7) (MSRP $1,300).
entries.quote: Highly detailed but with wonky treble, and requires a big head to couple correctly for the full bass presence.

entries.name: Grell OAE2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 7, Mids 7, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 5.6) (MSRP $599).
entries.quote: Exceptional bass and mids, sharp, sibilant treble, though that seems to vary dramatically from head to head.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-W2022
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 6, Comfort 6, Value 2.5) (MSRP $9,000).
entries.quote: Cloyingly warm and a bit dark sounding but still with decent internal coherence. Rotund midbass presence, decent mids but lacks clarity.

entries.name: ZMF Verite
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 7, Comfort 7, Value 3.9) (MSRP $2,500).
entries.quote: Punchy and can be very detailed on certain tracks but overall some wonky ear gain timbre and a consistent low treble emphasis.

entries.name: HIFIMAN Ananda
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.7/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 6.1) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: The original Ananda had a decent balance, but the newer ones seem to have a lot more treble to them in ways that make them a bit too bright.

entries.name: Hifiman sundara 2020
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.8/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 6.4) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: One of the more balanced all arounder sound signatures out there. Not particularly incisive but better mids than most other HiFiMAn headphones.

entries.name: Mark Levinson 5909
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.8/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 5) (MSRP $999).
entries.quote: Decent sounding ANC headphone let down slightly by overly fatiguing upper treble

entries.name: AUNE AR5000
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.6/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 8, Value 6.4) (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Comfort is great, nice warm midrange, treble is a bit low treble forward and scratchy but not unpalatable.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 580 precision
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 7, Value 6.9) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: This sounded like a more upper mids focused and slightly shoutier version of an HD 600.

entries.name: Audeze CRBN
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.7/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 4, Value 3.2) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: A somewhat darker and shoutier E-stat, also more midrange and ear gain focused than typical estats found elsewhere.

entries.name: DMS Omega
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 7, Value 5) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Good bass but slightly shouty ear gain and uneven treble presentation where the lower harmonics tend to dominate over upper ones.

entries.name: Aurorus Borealis
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.3/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 6, Value 5.1) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Punchy with a similar flaring effect to many of the Focal open back headphones but has a forward lower treble feature that stands out and skews the treble timbre

entries.name: ZMF Aeolus
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 7, Value 5) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Good bass extension, has a somewhat relaxed presentation but also some lower treble grain.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 560S
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.5/10 (Bass 5.5, Mids 6.5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 6.9) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Good bass extenssion for an open back and decent mids, treble gets a bit harsh with a low treble emphasis.

entries.name: HEDD Heddphone 2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 4, Mids 7, Treble 3, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 4.1) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Really good mids and it fixed the driver mode issue of the original, but at the cost of treble balance which is a bit harsh and uneven sounding for me.

entries.name: Hifiman Arya Stealth
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 7, Comfort 7, Value 5.7) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Great bass extension, dipped mids, spicy treble. It's a very spacious presentation but timbrally compromised as a result. It's a good demonstration of how the spaciousness effect imparts tradeoffs, but if that's what scores highly for you... it's a soundstage beast

entries.name: Sony Inzone H6 Air
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.9/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 2.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 9, Value 6.9) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Like a slightly worse MV-1 for have the price.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-R50x
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 5.4/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 6.9) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Decent v-shaped sound, good bass for an open back, also good mechanical design. I only wish the mids were a bit more present

entries.name: Meze 109 Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 5.6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 8, Value 5.2) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: Slight v-shape but still with present ear gain. Some uneven and gritty treble presentation but also reasonably incisive

entries.name: HIFIMAN EDITION XS
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 6.5) (MSRP $280).
entries.quote: The traditional HiFiMAN sound signature, good bass extension, dipped mids around 2khz, and then very present and clear treble with a peak around 9khz.

entries.name: Meze 99 classic v2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 6.2) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: A big improvement over the original, but too much treble in default mode and a bit blunted with the foam insert. Also has a strong dip around 4khz.

entries.name: Abyss Diana MR
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 3.6) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: One of the better Abyss models, but the treble timbre problems are once again its downfall.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 900 Pro X
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.3/10 (Bass 4, Mids 7, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 3, Value 6.5) (MSRP $279).
entries.quote: Probably the best sounding Beyerdynamic open back, still slightly shrill but solid mids.

entries.name: Bose QC Ultra
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 5.5/10 (Bass 3, Mids 7, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 8, Value 5.9) (MSRP $449).
entries.quote: Store-demo mode default sound signature with overdone bass and treble. But filters are in the right spots and sounds great when dialed in. Great midrange when primed with CustomTune

entries.name: Audeze LCD-GX
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 5) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Generally balanced with relaxed ear gain but treble still a bit disjointed.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD660s2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 5.7) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: A darker HD 650 with better bass extension.

entries.name: Moondrop Para 2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.5/10 (Bass 3, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 6, Comfort 4, Value 5.5) (MSRP $600).
entries.quote: Similar to Cosmo just with more treble, emphasizing the leanness. Incredible driver though and can be fantastic with a pad swap

entries.name: AKG K361
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 7.5) (MSRP $120).
entries.quote: Good bass, good mids, questionable treble, falls apart when you look at it the wrong way

entries.name: Fractal Design Scape (Fractal Scape Clarity)
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 4, Value 6.9) (MSRP $199).
entries.quote: V-shaped, leaning towards the treble. Decent sound signature for gaming, a bit too harsh for music. Thankfully comes with a PEQ app that integrates well with a button on the headphone.

entries.name: Meze Liric II
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.7/10, overall 4.8/10 (Bass 5, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 4.1) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: A big improvement over the original Liric but still too much upper treble

entries.name: Creative Aurvana
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.7/10, overall 4.5/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 10) (MSRP $15).
entries.quote: A classic closed back headphone with fun bouncy bass. Not amazing by modern standards but great value

entries.name: Meze Poet
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.7/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 4.1) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: One of the more normal sounding Meze headphones but for whatever reason it just doesn't work on my head. Not particularly incisive despite having a mostly decent balance to it.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Stealth
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.7/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 3.3) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Good on paper but sounds a bit shouty and strident to me. Lots of bass when it couples but also coupling sensitive.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-ADX7000
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.7/10, overall 5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 3.4) (MSRP $3,500).
entries.quote: 2 sets of pads, the more normal one sounds strident and congested, while the W shaped one sounds more incisive at the cost of sibilance and bass to midrange coherence.

entries.name: HarmonicDyne G200
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.7/10, overall 4.3/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 7, Comfort 3, Value 5.3) (MSRP $699).
entries.quote: It's a knock-off LCD-3 driver, which is capable just not tuned with enough ear gain. Absolutely cursed mechanical design

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 880
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.6/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 3, Mids 7, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 6.9) (MSRP $180).
entries.quote: Too bright, too lean. Solid midrange balance overall just tilted too much towards the treble for me.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-ADX5000
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.6/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 3.9) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: Just too bright for me. Not totally incoherent sounding just too much treble

entries.name: ZMF Atrium
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.6/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 7, Value 3.4) (MSRP $3,600).
entries.quote: Good bass and midrange, depending on the pads, but the treble has some stridency that I just can't get over.

entries.name: Phil Philphone
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.6/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 5.1) (MSRP $850).
entries.quote: Very punchy bass and some spicy treble. Good for electronic music but that's about all I like with it.

entries.name: HIFIMAN Arya Organic
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.6/10, overall 5.2/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 5) (MSRP $860).
entries.quote: U-shaped take on the HiFiMAN sound, tipping heavily towards the treble. It's too bright

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 660 S
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.5/10, overall 4.8/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 6.1) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Similar to the HD 660 S2, but not as well extended in the bass.

entries.name: Neumann NDH30
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.5/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 4, Comfort 7, Value 5.4) (MSRP $600).
entries.quote: Somewhat glaring around 4khz, otherwise unremarkable.

entries.name: Focal Elegia
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.4/10, overall 4.6/10 (Bass 5, Mids 2, Treble 5.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 5, Value 4.8) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Good bass when it couples correctly but glasses ruin this, quite wonky mids and ear gain, decent treble

entries.name: Sennheiser HD620s
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.4/10, overall 4.6/10 (Bass 4, Mids 3.5, Treble 5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 5, Value 6.1) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Boxy, honky midrange presentation. The ear gain and treble isn't bad for me, just that without EQ it can sound a bit like a phone booth.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 700 Pro X
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.4/10, overall 3.9/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 2, Value 6.4) (MSRP $270).
entries.quote: There's a hole in the ear gain between 3-5khz, but otherwise it's decently balanced overall, with a punchy bass emphasis and too much 5khz, because of the preceding dip. Not enough cup swivel

entries.name: Philips Fidelio X2HR
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.4/10, overall 4.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 3, Value 6.8) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: V-shaped. Grain Silo

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio Ether CX
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 3, Value 4.8) (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Good bass extension and decent mids but grainy treble

entries.name: Sony MDR-Z1R
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.7/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 2, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 4) (MSRP $1,900).
entries.quote: Solid bass and mids but the treble is very rough and imbalanced sounding to me, with some especially harsh upper treble.

entries.name: BeyerDynamic DT770
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.3/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 2, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 7) (MSRP $160).
entries.quote: It would be good if not for the treble sibilance. I actually liked versions of this headphone I've heard with worn pads, but most units I've heard have been sibilant

entries.name: Abyss 1266 Phi TC
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 3.6/10 (Bass 7, Mids 2, Treble 2, X-Factor 7, Comfort 1, Value 2.7) (MSRP $6,000).
entries.quote: Fun bass with a seal break but that's its party trick, very wonky otherwise. Extremely uncomfortable

entries.name: Fostex TRX00 Mahogany
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.2/10, overall 4.1/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 5, Comfort 4, Value 5.5) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Bassy, V-shaped, and the unit I heard had a 5khz peak of death.

entries.name: Meze Empyrean
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.2/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 6, Comfort 8, Value 3.5) (MSRP $3,000).
entries.quote: On first listen this is a nice lush kind of presentation, but it lacks a bit of clarity for the ear gain and there's too much distance between the mid and upper treble.

entries.name: Meze Strada
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.2/10, overall 5.1/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 2, X-Factor 5.5, Comfort 8, Value 5) (MSRP $799).
entries.quote: Like the Liric platform but lighter and more comfortable since it uses a dynamic driver. U-shaped with massive upper treble and some resonances throughout the ear gain. Can sound detailed but feels incoherent and disjointed.

entries.name: FiiO JT7
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.1/10, overall 4.9/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 7.5, Value 7.3) (MSRP $119).
entries.quote: A bit shouty and blunted sounding with default pads. FT1-B pads improve the response. Some distortion issues.

entries.name: ZMF Bokeh
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.1/10, overall 4.6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 6, Value 4.6) (MSRP $1,099).
entries.quote: Crazy bass punch but also too much treble glare - pad swaps may improve this but the default ones are a struggle for me.

entries.name: Apple AirPods Max
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.1/10, overall 3.7/10 (Bass 7, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 2, Value 5.4) (MSRP $549).
entries.quote: Great bass but mid to treble transition makes the treble unfortunately harsh sounding.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 569
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.1/10, overall 4.3/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 2, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5, Value 7) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Mids are okay but it's rather dull and blunted sounding in the treble.

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE4XX
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4/10, overall 4.2/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 6.9) (MSRP $160).
entries.quote: Nearly identical to HE400se, just without the rounded magnets, yielding slightly different upper treble.

entries.name: Hifiman HE400SE
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4/10, overall 4.2/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 7.4) (MSRP $110).
entries.quote: Decent bass extension at its price point, mids are dipped around 2khz, and there's a peak around 9khz. But for the price it's solid.

entries.name: Meze Liric
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4/10, overall 4.2/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3, Treble 4, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 3.9) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: Decent bass but there's a resonance in the mids that does weird things to vocals and general timbre.

entries.name: HiFiMAN Ananda Unveiled
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4/10, overall 4.3/10 (Bass 5, Mids 5.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5, Value 5.4) (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Just too lean. The wideband response seems like it would be good but there's an emphasis to the treble subjectively that makes it quite bright and treble focused

entries.name: Audeze LCD-2 Classic
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4/10, overall 4.2/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 5) (MSRP $800).
entries.quote: A more gritty take on the LCD-2 sound signature. Still emphasizing the warmth but with problematic treble.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-5
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 5, Comfort 6, Value 3) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: Honky mids with very little ear gain. Too far in the other direction compared to the LCD-5. At least they fixed the clamp force issue.

entries.name: Koss KPH30i
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.9/10, overall 4.1/10 (Bass 2, Mids 5, Treble 5, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5, Value 8.6) (MSRP $40).
entries.quote: One of the more complete on-ear headphones. Still suffers from bass roll off due to the nature of this design, but totally acceptable for the price.

entries.name: Sennheiser HD 820
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.9/10, overall 4.8/10 (Bass 2, Mids 2, Treble 5, X-Factor 6, Comfort 8, Value 3.8) (MSRP $2,200).
entries.quote: Very strange bass and midrange transition, it has this low frequency booming tonal resonance while also sounding hollow and lean at the same time. I think when I first started getting into headphones I was drawn to the build and design, because it does look cool. But the sound is not competitive.

entries.name: Philips SHP9500
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.9/10, overall 4.6/10 (Bass 3, Mids 4, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 5, Comfort 7, Value 7.5) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Shifted ear gain towards the treble, compromising on timbre in favor of grain

entries.name: beyerdynamic TYGR 300R
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.9/10, overall 4.1/10 (Bass 3, Mids 5.5, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 6.7) (MSRP $180).
entries.quote: Some unit variation. Treble is not as insane as some other Beyers, but the bass is also quite blooming in the upper and mid bass.

entries.name: Aurorus Australis
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.9/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 6, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 6, Value 4.8) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Overly warmed, stiffled and lacking clarity, but could be good for those who are treble averse.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-R30x
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 3.8/10 (Bass 2, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 4, Value 7.4) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Doesn't couple to the head sufficiently for any low frequency content. Just bright and shrill.

entries.name: FiiO FT13
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 4.4/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 2, X-Factor 2, Comfort 6, Value 6) (MSRP $330).
entries.quote: The bass and mids are okay but really rough and strident treble. The alternative pads make the treble a bit better but bass becomes absurdly huge. Also doesn't properly couple to the side of the head.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT1990 Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 3.6/10 (Bass 6, Mids 6, Treble 1, X-Factor 3, Comfort 3, Value 5.9) (MSRP $360).
entries.quote: Great bass extension, solid midrange, but marred by two peaks of death at 8.5khz and 12khz. Extremely sibilant

entries.name: ZMF Atrium Closed
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.7/10, overall 4.3/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3, Treble 4, X-Factor 3, Comfort 6, Value 3.5) (MSRP $2,600).
entries.quote: Every time I listen to this headphone it just sounds shouty and dull to me. There may be some pads that help, but I haven't heard them.

entries.name: T Plus A Solitaire T
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.7/10, overall 3.5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 6, Treble 3, X-Factor 2, Comfort 3, Value 4) (MSRP $1,600).
entries.quote: Default sound signature resembles a front-biased sound field skewing treble response for headphones. This yields a very strange timbre profile as a result.

entries.name: Sony MDR-7506
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.7/10, overall 4/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5, Value 7.4) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Lean and strident, but otherwise acceptable midrange.

entries.name: Denon AH-D9200
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.7/10, overall 4.2/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3, Treble 3, X-Factor 4, Comfort 6, Value 4.1) (MSRP $1,500).
entries.quote: An incoherent take on neutral closed back. The ear gain presentation and treble sounds very strange.

entries.name: Moondrop Horizon
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.7/10, overall 4/10 (Bass 4, Mids 5, Treble 2, X-Factor 4, Comfort 5, Value 6.5) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Just too dark in the treble, while also being harsh at the same time.

entries.name: Meze 105 Silva
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.6/10, overall 4.6/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 2, X-Factor 4, Comfort 8, Value 5.4) (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Kind of between the 105 AER and the 109 Pro, but with too much contrast between mid and upper treble with a strong upper treble zing.

entries.name: RAAL Immanis
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.6/10, overall 3.9/10 (Bass 5, Mids 3, Treble 1, X-Factor 6, Comfort 5, Value 2.1) (MSRP $9,000).
entries.quote: Bass was okay but the mids sounded a bit incoherent with a forwardness around 1khz and then dipped for the ear gain, and then an absolutely murderous treble resonance on my head every time I hear this one.

entries.name: HIFIMAN HE5XX
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.5/10, overall 3.8/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5, Value 6.4) (MSRP $220).
entries.quote: Acoustically the same as the Deva

entries.name: HIFIMAN Deva (wired)
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.5/10, overall 3.8/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 5, Value 6) (MSRP $299).
entries.quote: Warmer than other HiFiMANs but blunted and fuzzy sounding overall.

entries.name: Rode NTH-100
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.5/10, overall 3.6/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4, Value 6.8) (MSRP $159).
entries.quote: Muffled, congested sound, not incisive. Overly intimate

entries.name: Meze 105 Aer
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.4/10, overall 4.5/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 2, X-Factor 3, Comfort 8, Value 5.6) (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Bassier open back marred by grainy ear gain and harsh treble.

entries.name: Audeze CRBN2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.3/10, overall 3.2/10 (Bass 3, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 3, Value 2.7) (MSRP $4,500).
entries.quote: Considerably worse than the original CRBN. More prominent bass but everything else got worse somehow.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic DT 990 (600 Ohm)
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.3/10, overall 3.4/10 (Bass 4, Mids 7, Treble 0, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4, Value 6.6) (MSRP $170).
entries.quote: Some of the most instane treble I've ever encountered. The mids are actually quite good, and it has some bass, but the treble is murderous.

entries.name: AKG K712 PRO
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.2/10, overall 3.3/10 (Bass 2, Mids 2, Treble 5, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4, Value 5.7) (MSRP $350).
entries.quote: Rolled off bass and super wonky midrange presentation. Treble isn't bad. Problematic mechanical design with difficulty coupling correctly.

entries.name: Philips SHP9600
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.2/10, overall 3.8/10 (Bass 3, Mids 3, Treble 3.5, X-Factor 3, Comfort 6, Value 7.6) (MSRP $75).
entries.quote: More bloated bass, worse mids, similar grain as previous version

entries.name: Koss KSC75
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.1/10, overall 3.5/10 (Bass 2, Mids 4, Treble 4, X-Factor 2, Comfort 5, Value 8.6) (MSRP $30).
entries.quote: Aggressive bass roll off, decent mids but harsh lower treble

entries.name: Koss Porta Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.1/10, overall 3.5/10 (Bass 2, Mids 5, Treble 3, X-Factor 2, Comfort 5, Value 8) (MSRP $50).
entries.quote: Similar to KSC75 just with worse treble and more tubby upper bass bloom.

entries.name: Audio-Technica ATH-M50x
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.1/10, overall 3.2/10 (Bass 2, Mids 4, Treble 3, X-Factor 3, Comfort 4, Value 6.7) (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Bassy, bloomy, muddy, blunted, fuzzy.

entries.name: Fostex T50RP Mk3
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3/10, overall 3.5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 3, Treble 3, X-Factor 2, Comfort 5, Value 6.3) (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Clangy mids and harsh, strident treble.

entries.name: Audeze LCD-2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.9/10, overall 2.5/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 2, X-Factor 2, Comfort 1, Value 4.4) (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: Very heavy, and overall very strange kind of sound signature. The bass felt very articulate but that's about all I could enjoy with it.

entries.name: Grell Audio OAE1
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.9/10, overall 2.9/10 (Bass 4, Mids 4, Treble 1, X-Factor 3, Comfort 3, Value 6) (MSRP $249).
entries.quote: Overly bassy, dark and shouty with extremely strange treble timbre.

entries.name: Dan Clark Audio EXPANSE
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.6/10, overall 3.6/10 (Bass 5, Mids 4, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 7, Value 2.7) (MSRP $4,000).
entries.quote: Bassy open back but also shouty and harsh treble with upper treble roll off. The AMTS didn't work for me on this one.

entries.name: B&O H100
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.6/10, overall 3/10 (Bass 6.5, Mids 3, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 4, Value 3.7) (MSRP $1,549).
entries.quote: Good bass. Mids are a bit wonky and treble is very rough. Poorly integrated ear gain balance.

entries.name: Grado SR325x
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.5/10, overall 2.4/10 (Bass 2, Mids 3, Treble 2, X-Factor 3, Comfort 2, Value 5.6) (MSRP $295).
entries.quote: Similar to other Grados with a massive 2khz resonance, just slightly better bass extension and not as peaky for the rest of the treble.

entries.name: Moondrop Edge
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.5/10, overall 3/10 (Bass 6, Mids 3, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 4, Value 7.2) (MSRP $80).
entries.quote: Dark and shouty, atrocious mids and treble presentation with a meaningful ear gain imbalance. But the app has PEQ, so it can be made to sound great.

entries.name: Bowers & Wilkins Px8
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.2/10, overall 2.4/10 (Bass 3, Mids 3, Treble 2, X-Factor 1, Comfort 3, Value 4.3) (MSRP $749).
entries.quote: Overly boomy, muddy bass, can be reduced in the app but then reveals how wonky the rest of the sound signature is.

entries.name: Beyerdynamic Aventho 300 Wireless
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.2/10, overall 2.6/10 (Bass 4, Mids 2, Treble 2, X-Factor 1, Comfort 4, Value 5.1) (MSRP $399).
entries.quote: One of the worst sounding wireless headphones available. Essentially the opposite of what ear gain balance should be. Congested and harsh at the same time.

entries.name: HarmonicDyne Poseidon
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 2.1/10, overall 3/10 (Bass 2, Mids 1, Treble 3, X-Factor 2, Comfort 6, Value 4.9) (MSRP $439).
entries.quote: Blunted and bloated while also having bass roll off. Likely the worst of this platform.

entries.name: Hifiman sundara closed
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 1.9/10, overall 2.1/10 (Bass 2, Mids 2, Treble 1.5, X-Factor 2, Comfort 3, Value 6.3) (MSRP $129).
entries.quote: Just an absolute nightmare rollercoaster of doom.

entries.name: beyerdynamic DT 990 Pro X
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 1.9/10, overall 2.6/10 (Bass 1.5, Mids 4, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 5, Value 5.7) (MSRP $199).
entries.quote: Lean and shrill. At least the mids were okay, but it made me not want to listen to music.

entries.name: Grado SR60x
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 1.7/10, overall 1.8/10 (Bass 2, Mids 2, Treble 1, X-Factor 2, Comfort 2, Value 6.4) (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: It's mostly just massive treble resonances and terrible build quality.

entries.name: HIFIMAN Audivina
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 1/10, overall 1.7/10 (Bass 1, Mids 1, Treble 1, X-Factor 1, Comfort 4, Value 2.3) (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: The thing that goes bump in the night...

entries.name: Harmonicdyne X Zeos Eris
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 0.9/10, overall 1.9/10 (Bass 2, Mids 1, Treble 0, X-Factor 1, Comfort 5, Value 4.6) (MSRP $249).
entries.quote: It's only as bad as it sounds

entries.name: CrinEar Reference
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 7.4/10, overall 7.5/10 (MSRP $349).
entries.quote: One of the few actually neutral IEMs to exist. Well-textured and tonally rich bass, great midrange, and balanced treble just with a hint of forwardness around 4.5khz.

entries.name: Moondrop x Crinacle: Dusk DSP Default
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 7/10, overall 6.3/10 (MSRP $330).
entries.quote: One of the best if not the best sounding IEMs for me, but downside is the DSP cable has its issues.

entries.name: SUBTONIC STORM
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.5/10, overall 5/10 (MSRP $6,000).
entries.quote: A surprisingly balanced sound signature overall, lovely midrange, just too much mid and upper treble.

entries.name: 64 Audio U6t
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 5.7/10 (MSRP $1,300).
entries.quote: Probably my favorite of the 64 Audio IEMs, more balanced than the rest with just a touch of flare to make it exciting.

entries.name: Prisma Lumen
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 5.3/10 (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Doesn't totally fix the length mode issue I get with this IEM but dramatically improves it.

entries.name: ThieAudio Oracle MK1
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.3/10, overall 5.8/10 (MSRP $539).
entries.quote: Just solid all around, useful as a reference set. Normal in the best of ways.

entries.name: Shuoer Cadenza 12
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (MSRP $2,300).
entries.quote: Really solid tuning for most of it, well-balanced. Slightly forward low to mid treble, but otherwise really enjoyable.

entries.name: 64 Audio U12t
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.4/10 (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: A warm and relaxed yet highly detailed and incisive IEM. Notable 3khz dip. Slightly too much upper treble for me

entries.name: Hisenior Mega 5 EST
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.2/10 (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: A trend-setter, defining the 'new meta' sound signature. Mostly balanced overall just with too much upper treble, not enough mid treble.

entries.name: Prisma Lux
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 6/10, overall 5.2/10 (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Tasteful V-shape. A more grandiose sound than Lumen, with similarly great midrange. Ear gain as Lumen but the extra mid and upper treble balances it better

entries.name: CRINEAR DAYBREAK
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 6.1/10 (MSRP $170).
entries.quote: One of the easiest recommendations for IEMs generally, but only with the coffee tips (they may be included now)

entries.name: Empire Ears Odin
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 4.8/10 (MSRP $3,399).
entries.quote: Highly incisive but too much bloom around 2khz making it a bit on the lean side of things.

entries.name: Hisenior Mega7
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 5.5/10 (MSRP $449).
entries.quote: More coherent mids and ear gain than the Mega5 but poorly-integrated sub bass and upper treble. Just too much on both ends.

entries.name: NICEHCK ROCKIES
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 5.4/10 (MSRP $470).
entries.quote: A brighter take on the new meta sound signature, unfortunately a bit too bright. But very close to being great.

entries.name: Softears Volume S
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 5.6/10 (MSRP $320).
entries.quote: Intense, thunderous bass that's satisfying but marred by incoherent and poorly integrated midrange.

entries.name: ThieAudio Monarch MKII
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.8/10, overall 5.1/10 (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Typical neutral with a bass boost, a more expressive and vivid presentation that's mostly palatable.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears KE4
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.6/10, overall 5.7/10 (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Similar to Mega5EST, just with too much bloom into the low mids for the more relaxed ear gain presentation, which also makes it sound a bit too dull.

entries.name: CrinEar Project Meta
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.9/10 (MSRP $250).
entries.quote: Similar to the Daybreak with coffee tips, exceptional midrange, just more disjointed low bass and upper treble

entries.name: DUNU x Gizaudio Davinci
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.3/10 (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Overly warm and bassy, but balanced for the rest of it.

entries.name: Symphonium Crimson
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 4.8/10 (MSRP $1,200).
entries.quote: Way too much upper treble for me but solid for the rest of it.

entries.name: Symphonium x Nightjar Meteor
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.2/10 (MSRP $600).
entries.quote: A relaxed, bassy presentation. Too much upper treble, but otherwise works very well.

entries.name: TruthEar Hexa
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.5/10, overall 5.7/10 (MSRP $90).
entries.quote: A slightly brighter take on neutral. Too much low treble with a bit of glare but otherwise really great

entries.name: 64 Audio Tia Trio
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.4/10, overall 4.9/10 (MSRP $2,300).
entries.quote: A fun v-shaped sound with some flare that makes it vivid and exciting.

entries.name: 64 Audio U4s
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.1/10 (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: Similar to the U12t just not quite as tasteful. Hint of clang in the mids, though treble may be more balanced

entries.name: Apple AirPods Pro 2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.1/10 (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: The default go-to competent all rounder TWS. It's balanced across the board with great sounding mids. Treble could be more refined

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Quintet
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 5.1/10 (MSRP $220).
entries.quote: Somewhat shouty with low treble glare, but decent bass punch and otherwise balanced

entries.name: Softears RSV mk2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 4.9/10 (MSRP $700).
entries.quote: High contrast kind of sound signature with lots of bass and ear gain, but too much to sound balanced, low treble glare.

entries.name: Sony IER-Z1R
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 3.9/10 (MSRP $1,700).
entries.quote: Crazy bass quality and texture but not amazing for the rest of it, and has treble issues.

entries.name: ThieAudio Hype 4
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.3/10, overall 4.9/10 (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: Too much upper treble but otherwise a mostly fun and vivid sound signature that doesn't stray too far from normal - decent mids.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE600
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.3/10 (MSRP $900).
entries.quote: V-shaped, sibilant, but satisfying bass

entries.name: XENNS Tea PRO
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5.1/10, overall 5.1/10 (MSRP $360).
entries.quote: Bassy, W-shaped sound signature with more forward 2khz presence.

entries.name: DUNU Glacier
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.2/10 (MSRP $1,350).
entries.quote: V-shaped, somewhat Harmanlike, crazy bass. Really large and heavy shells

entries.name: DUNU Mirai
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.7/10 (MSRP $950).
entries.quote: Similar sound to some of the 64 Audio IEMs in the ear gain but with treble that works less good for me.

entries.name: DUNU SA6
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.7/10 (MSRP $550).
entries.quote: Relaxed, warm, non-fatiguing sound with clarity-focused midrange

entries.name: I/O Sogno
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5/10 (MSRP $400).
entries.quote: A Harman IE-like sound signature, just too shouty. But it's better than most for this type of tuning.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE 200
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.6/10 (MSRP $160).
entries.quote: Somehow the most balanced of this series, but still a bit grainy and scratchy sounding.

entries.name: TruthEar Pure
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.5/10 (MSRP $90).
entries.quote: Like the Hexa but with better treble and muddier upper bass and low mids.

entries.name: TruthEar ZERO RED
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 5.3/10 (MSRP $55).
entries.quote: The much better and more balanced version of this IEM

entries.name: Xenns Top Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 5/10, overall 4.9/10 (MSRP $500).
entries.quote: Bassy with more forward ear gain presence, yielding a more detailed presentation than the typical meta tunings. Somewhat incoherent treble.

entries.name: DUNU Titan S2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 4.5/10 (MSRP $80).
entries.quote: Harmanlike without the low mid scoop. A bit too much low treble focus but good otherwise

entries.name: Moondrop Blessing 3
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 5/10 (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: V-shaped, punchy bass, lean mids, emphasized ear gain.

entries.name: Moondrop KATO
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 5.1/10 (MSRP $190).
entries.quote: Solid, punchy bass. Treble is a bit problematic and mids slightly lean.

entries.name: Sennheiser IE 900
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.9/10, overall 4.6/10 (MSRP $1,700).
entries.quote: Wonky midrange, but bass hits like a truck

entries.name: 7Hz Timeless
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.7/10 (MSRP $220).
entries.quote: Mostly balanced just with harshness in the treble. Surprisingly detailed

entries.name: Campfire Andromeda 2020
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.5/10 (MSRP $1,100).
entries.quote: Slightly incoherent mid to treble balance. Relaxed ear gain, but mid and upper treble is okay for me.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Orchestra Lite
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4.8/10 (MSRP $250).
entries.quote: Relaxed, non-fatiguing treble, slightly congested by otherwise decent, honky mids.

entries.name: Moondrop x Crinacle Blessing2 Dusk
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.8/10, overall 4/10 (MSRP $320).
entries.quote: The analog sound signature is rather peaky in the treble, but the rest of it is okay.

entries.name: Prisma Lumen
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.6/10, overall 4.1/10 (MSRP $1,400).
entries.quote: Fantastic midrange but simultaneously glaring yet blunted treble. Let down by anemic bass, rather punishing lower treble that dominates over the rest of the response.

entries.name: 64 Audio Nio
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.5/10, overall 4.4/10 (MSRP $1,700).
entries.quote: Can be overly bassy depending on the module, but otherwise enjoyable sound signature.

entries.name: Crinear Monolith
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.5/10, overall 5.3/10 (MSRP $399).
entries.quote: Truly ridiculous levels of bass that drowns out what is otherwise an acceptable midrange and ear gain presentation. I'd say this is the meta-tuning for bassheads but the treble is also a bit rocky. I feel Crin is trolling me with this one.

entries.name: Meze Astru
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.4/10, overall 4.7/10 (MSRP $899).
entries.quote: W-shaped sound signature with good bass, quirky mids and emphasized treble. Too much uppy-downy treble, with dominante lower treble harmonics.

entries.name: Audiosense DT200
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.7/10 (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Mostly neutral but a bit too bright and lean

entries.name: Empire Ears Legend EVO
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 3.5/10 (MSRP $3,100).
entries.quote: V-shaped with intense bass and forward 2khz presence. Can sometimes be vivid and exciting but very timbrally compromised.

entries.name: Etymotic ER2XR
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.2/10 (MSRP $105).
entries.quote: Like the 2SE just with more bass.

entries.name: Moondrop Variations
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.3/10 (MSRP $540).
entries.quote: Good bass but an absolute shout-fiesta. Low treble glare for days.

entries.name: TruthEar Nova
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.6/10 (MSRP $150).
entries.quote: Harman IE-like, V-shaped with solid bass but fatiguing ear gain and low treble.

entries.name: ZIIGAAT ARCANIS
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4.3/10, overall 4.5/10 (MSRP $300).
entries.quote: Non-fatiguing, but wonky ear gain and low treble.

entries.name: ThieAudio Monarch MKIII
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 4/10, overall 3.8/10 (MSRP $1,000).
entries.quote: The more V-shaped version, just too unnatural sounding with a leaner midrange presentation and worse treble

entries.name: 64 Audio Volür
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 3.8/10 (MSRP $2,000).
entries.quote: V-shaped. It does the spaciousness thing quite well but the upper treble is so unreasonably spicy for me, I struggled with this one.

entries.name: 7Hz Salnotes Dioko
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 4/10 (MSRP $100).
entries.quote: Rough, peaky treble. It could be incisve but usually comes across rather strident.

entries.name: Apple AirPods Pro 3
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 3.9/10 (MSRP $250).
entries.quote: More v-shaped, Harman IE adjacent, absolutely intolerable length mode problems. The treble just sucks on these.

entries.name: Etymotic ER2SE
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 3.9/10 (MSRP $105).
entries.quote: A bit lean and shouty for me. Unpleasant insertion depth, but it's also beneficial for killing low treble resonances

entries.name: Kiwi Ears Quartet
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.8/10, overall 4.2/10 (MSRP $110).
entries.quote: Too much bloom in the low mids for this kind of ear gain.

entries.name: 7Hz Salnotes Zero:2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.6/10, overall 4.1/10 (MSRP $20).
entries.quote: Similar to the original zero just with better bass. Treble is still a problem.

entries.name: Apple AirPods Pro
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.6/10, overall 4/10 (MSRP $200).
entries.quote: Made sense for its time, but slightly lean and boring sounding.

entries.name: Kiwi Ears x Crinacle Singolo
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.5/10, overall 3.9/10 (MSRP $79).
entries.quote: Shifted ear gain towards low treble yields a leaner midrange profile, along with punishing glare, despite good sounding bass.

entries.name: ZIIGAAT LUSH
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.5/10, overall 3.9/10 (MSRP $180).
entries.quote: Slow, soft, pillow low frequency presence with harsh and unnatural timbre

entries.name: 7Hz Salnotes Zero
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.4/10, overall 4/10 (MSRP $20).
entries.quote: Would be good if it didn't have the most punishing lower treble and length mode resonance issues. Problematic shell design

entries.name: Creative Aurvana Ace 2
entries.verdict: Resolve rates sound 3.3/10, overall 3.7/10 (MSRP $80).
entries.quote: Bass and mids are decent but the treble is punishing with a shift towards the low treble band.

entries.name: Truthear Zero
